entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hon'Ble Sri Justice C.V.Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.3207 of 2023
O R D E R:

This writ petition is filed seeking the following relief:
"......to issue Writ Order or Direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the Respondent Nos 2 and 3 in interfering with civil disputes between the petitioner and 4th respondent as illegal arbitrary contrary to law and violative of constitutional mandates guaranteed under the Constitution of India and pass......"

2. Learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner had entered into agreement of sale dated 01.03.2004 with one Durdana Unnisa for purchasing the open plot admeasuring 320 Sq yards in Sy.No.58 situated at Himayath Nagar, Hyderabad for a total sale consideration of Rs.9,50,000/-.

He submits that since the petitioner's vendor has not come forward to execute the registered Sale Deed, the petitioner has issued a legal notice dated 23.09.2004 and thereafter filed a suit vide O.S.No.71 of 2005 on the file of V Senior Civil Judge, City Civil Court,
Hyderabad, for specific performance of agreement of sale and the trial Court, after contesting the matter has executed a registered Sale Deed vide registered Sale Deed No.1943 of 2008, dated 07.04.2007.

entities.text:
Senior Civil Judge, City Civil Court,
Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He submits that during the pendency of the said suit, on the complaint made by respondent No.4, respondent No.3 is frequently interfering into the civil disputes between the petitioner and respondent No.4 and calling the petitioner to the Police Station and made him to sit hours together and also directed him to settle the civil disputes with respondent No.4.

He submits that respondent No.3 is neither having any power or authority to intervene into the civil disputes between the petitioner and respondent No.4 nor directing them to settle the disputes.
3.

This Court vide order dated 03.02.2023 permitted the petitioner to take out personal notice to respondent No.4 and also directed respondent No.3 not to interfere in the civil disputes pending between the petitioner and respondent No.4 without following due process of law.

4. Learned Assistant Government Pleader appearing for Home submits that respondent No.3 has received a complaint from respondent No.4 against the petitioner and as the said complaint disclosed the cognizable offence, respondent No.3 has registered a crime vide F.I.R. No.17 of 2021 under Section 420 r/w Section 24 of Indian Penal Code and after conducting investigation, he has also laid a charge sheet before the competent Court.
He submits that respondent No.3 has neither interfered with the civil disputes of the petitioner nor directed him to settle the civil disputes with respondent No.4.

sentences.text: 1 5. Recording the submissions made by learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home, this Court deems it appropriate to dispose of this writ petition, directing respondent No.3 not to interfere with the civil disputes between the petitioner and respondent No.4, in any manner, except in accordance with law.
Further, if the presence of the petitioner is necessary for further investigation of the said crime, respondent No.3 is at liberty to take appropriate steps, in accordance with law.
6. Accordingly, this writ petition is disposed of.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.

JUSTICE C.V.BHASKAR REDDY Date:
